name: Jenkins
description: Jenkins is an open-source automation server for continuous integration and delivery, with a large plugin ecosystem for building, testing, deploying, and automating software projects.
best_for: Best suited to teams that want a free, highly extensible CI/CD server and are prepared to operate the Jenkins controller, agents, plugins, upgrades, backups, and security themselves.
features: Hundreds of plugins for source control, build, test, deployment, and notification workflows
Web-based configuration with built-in help and validation
Distributed builds across multiple agents and platforms
Pipeline-as-code for defining delivery workflows in version control
Self-contained Java application with packages for major operating systems
Open-source Jenkins core under the MIT License

alternatives.name: CircleCI
alternatives.description: A cloud, self-hosted-runner, and on-premise CI/CD platform for building, testing, and deploying software.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want a managed CI/CD platform without maintaining their own server.

alternatives.name: GitLab
alternatives.description: An end-to-end DevSecOps platform spanning planning through deployment and security.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations wanting source control and CI/CD in one consolidated platform.

alternatives.name: GitHub
alternatives.description: A developer platform for hosting code and automating workflows via GitHub Actions.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want CI/CD built directly into the same platform that hosts their code.

tiers.name: Jenkins core
tiers.notes: Independent open-source project; core uses the MIT License.

cons: Jenkins core is free, but infrastructure, storage, build agents, backups, monitoring, and administrator time are separate operating costs.
The Jenkins project does not sell a managed SaaS tier with a vendor SLA; teams either operate Jenkins themselves or buy hosting/support from third parties.
A heavily customized plugin stack increases the amount of compatibility and upgrade testing your team owns.

faq.question: Is Jenkins free?
faq.answer: Yes. Jenkins core is open source under the MIT License and has no software license fee. Your organization still pays for the infrastructure, storage, build agents, administration, and support model it chooses.

faq.question: Does Jenkins offer a managed cloud plan?
faq.answer: The Jenkins project itself does not sell a managed SaaS tier. Organizations can self-host Jenkins or use commercial hosting and support services from third parties.

faq.question: What should I inventory before migrating away from Jenkins?
faq.answer: Inventory pipelines, Jenkinsfiles, plugins, credentials, agents, shared libraries, triggers, artifacts, secrets, and external integrations. Rebuild and test those workflows on the target CI/CD platform before disabling production jobs.

faq.question: What operating systems can run Jenkins?
faq.answer: Jenkins is a Java-based server with packages and installation paths for Windows, macOS, Linux, and other Unix-like systems.
